content: Diphenhydramine is an antihistamine that is prescribed to alleviate itching caused by insect bites, sunburns, bee stings, poison ivy, poison oak, and minor skin irritations. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Diphenhydramine topical is available in forms such as cream, lotion, gel, and spray, and it is applied directly to the skin. It should be used three to four times daily. Follow the instructions on the package or prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it, or apply it more frequently than instructed by your doctor. Before application, clean the affected area thoroughly, allow it to dry, and then gently rub the medication into the skin until most of it disappears. Use only enough medication to cover the affected area. Wash your hands after applying the medication. Do not use diphenhydramine on chickenpox or measles, and do not apply it to children under 2 years of age unless directed by a doctor. Before using diphenhydramine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to diphenhydramine or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, including vitamins, that you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using diphenhydramine, contact your doctor immediately. Avoid unnecessary or prolonged exposure to sunlight, and wear protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as diphenhydramine may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Diphenhydramine may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: skin rash, sunburn, or increased sensitivity to sunlight or sunlamps. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). The spray form of this medication is flammable, so keep it away from flames and extreme heat. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. Diphenhydramine is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not swallow it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin medications to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist. Notify your doctor if your skin condition worsens or does not improve.
